Title: Main Debugging Detective
Role: Your task is to find the buggy method. You have static tools to read code and a special dynamic verification tool.

Workflow:
1. Prioritize Error Analysis: If a stack trace is provided, start by investigating the deepest method in the trace that belongs to the target project. This is often where the bug or the symptom manifests.
2. Static Exploration: Use static tools (get_code_snippet, etc.) to read the code at the identified suspicious locations. Pay close attention to variable calculations and boundary conditions (especially for IndexOutOfBounds errors).
3. Hypothesis Formulation: Form a specific hypothesis about the root cause (e.g., "Line 95 performs a double increment on the index, causing an overflow").
4. Dynamic Verification (Recommended): Call `nominate_suspicious_method` to verify your hypothesis with runtime data.
   - Specify `variables_of_interest` that are involved in the failing condition (e.g., loop counters, index variables, or null-check targets).
   - The sub-agent will provide ground-truth runtime values to confirm or refute your hypothesis.
   - If the verification report says NO_BUG or INCONCLUSIVE, consider investigating other methods or re-nominating with different `target_lines`.
   - You may nominate multiple methods if you have several plausible hypotheses.

Goal: Provide the final diagnosis based on the available evidence (static and/or dynamic).

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

" *

Copies the given array and adds the given element at the end of the new array.

* *

The new array contains the same elements of the input * array plus the given element in the last position. The component type of * the new array is the same as that of the input array.

* *

If the input array is null, a new one element array is returned * whose component type is the same as the element, unless the element itself is null, * in which case the return type is Object[]

* * 
     * ArrayUtils.add(null, null)      = [null]
     * ArrayUtils.add(null, "a")       = ["a"]
     * ArrayUtils.add(["a"], null)     = ["a", null]
     * ArrayUtils.add(["a"], "b")      = ["a", "b"]
     * ArrayUtils.add(["a", "b"], "c") = ["a", "b", "c"]
     *
* * @param array the array to "add" the element to, may be null * @param element the object to add, may be null * @return A new array containing the existing elements plus the new element * The returned array type will be that of the input array (unless null), * in which case it will have the same type as the element. * If both are null, an IllegalArgumentException is thrown * @since 2.1 * @throws IllegalArgumentException if both arguments are null "

" * Returns a copy of the given array of size 1 greater than the argument. * The last value of the array is left to the default value. * * @param array The array to copy, must not be null. * @param newArrayComponentType If array is null, create a * size 1 array of this type. * @return A new copy of the array of size 1 greater than the input. "

The bug is in:

`org.apache.commons.lang3.ArrayUtils.add(T[], T)`

Diagnosis:
- The failing test calls `ArrayUtils.add(null, null)` with target type `String[]`.
- The method currently does:
  - if `array != null` => use array type
  - else if `element != null` => use element type
  - else => `type = Object.class`
- So when both arguments are `null`, it creates an `Object[]` via `copyArrayGrow1(array, type)`.
- That `Object[]` is then cast to `T[]`, which at runtime becomes a cast from `Object[]` to `String[]`, causing the observed `ClassCastException`.

This contradicts the method’s own JavaDoc, which explicitly says:
- “If both are null, an IllegalArgumentException is thrown”

So the root cause is that `ArrayUtils.add(T[], T)` handles the `(array == null && element == null)` case incorrectly by creating an `Object[]` instead of throwing `IllegalArgumentException`.

`copyArrayGrow1(java.lang.Object, java.lang.Class<?>)` is not the primary bug source here; it behaves consistently with the type it is given. The incorrect decision is made in `add(T[], T)`.

SYSTEM ALERT: You explained your thoughts but did not output a valid tool call. 
- If you need to examine code or verify a hypothesis, you MUST explicitly invoke a function (e.g., `get_code_snippet`, `nominate_suspicious_method`).
- If you have completely finished the investigation and are ready to provide the final buggy method signature, reply EXACTLY with the word 'READY'.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
